items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S3656

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the arts and cultural affairs law, in relation to
participation of trustees of the board of trustees of the Trust for
Cultural Resources of the city of New York who concurrently serve as
ex officio officers or board members of a participating cultural
institution and the designation of a representative by the
commissioner of cultural affairs of the city of New York to attend and
vote at meetings of the board of trustees of the Trust for Cultural
Resources


 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

section 1 of the bill amends subdivision 3 of § 21.05 of the Arts and
Cultural Affairs Law by providing that any person serving ex officio
as a member of the board of trustees of the Trust for Cultural
Resources of the city of New York (the "Trust") may also serve
concurrently as an ex officio member of the board of trustees, or the
equivalent body, of a participating cultural institution, providing
that no more than one such person serves in other than an ex officio
capacity. Further, such ex officio member of the board of trustees and
of the participating cultural institution may participate in
discussions and voting on matters pertaining to the participating
cultural institution.

Section 2 of the bill adds subdivision 4 of § 21.05 of the Arts and
Cultural Affairs Law by amending the title of the Deputy Mayor for
Economic Development and Rebuilding and by authorizing the city's
Commissioner of Cultural Affairs (the "Commissioner") as an ex-officio
member of the board of trustees of the Trust to designate a person to
attend and vote at meetings of the board of trustees from which he or
she may be absent. Section 3 specifies that the act shall take effect
immediately.

The Trust provides tax-exempt bonds, the proceeds of which benefit
not-for-profit cultural institutions in supporting capital
development, expansion or improvement projects. The Trust serves as an
invaluable resource to the City's non-profit cultural organizations by
supporting the restoration of landmark properties and significant
construction development projects.

 REASONS FOR SUPPORT :

Allowing the Commissioner to serve as an ex officio member of the
board of trustees while concurrently serving on the board of trustees
of the participating cultural institution will enhance the Trust's
consideration of proposed development projects. The Commissioner
oversees and coordinates the City's funding for cultural programs and
capital projects, and thus has a unique and comprehensive
understanding of the City's cultural organizations and their capacity
for project undertakings. In turn, the Commissioner is able to provide
valuable insight to the Trust's board of trustees in determining the
impact and consequences of proposed improvements and development.

Further, the limitation on concurrent board service in subdivision 3
of § 20.09 of the Arts and Cultural Affairs Law was designed to
address potential conflicts of interest for non-ex officio trustees
serving on the board of trustees of both participating cultural
institutions and the Trust. Although non-ex officio trustees of all
cultural institutions are required to serve in the public interest, to
avoid the appearance of self-interest, the Trust's enabling
legislation required that non-ex officio trustees refrain from
participating or voting on matters for which they have a duty of
loyalty to a cultural institution that is seeking financing from the
Trust. However, the rationale for prohibiting the participation of
members of a participating cultural institution's board in the
deliberations of the Trust's board is not applicable to a trustee
serving ex officio such as the Commissioner. The Commissioner serves
as on the board of trustees in an ex officio capacity solely for the
purpose of representing the mayoral administration in which the
Commissioner serves and, therefore, no personal allegiance or conflict
of interest exists.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
There is no fiscal impact.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This bill shall take effect immediately.
